points.t: Asian Games 2026: India finishes 4th with 85 medals after golden Day 15
points.s: India closed the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on October 3 with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze (85 total), finishing fourth overall. Historic golds: 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod (first Indian woman to win individual recurve archery gold, beating South Korea's Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off, and an LA 2028 quota) and Pranavi Urs (first Indian woman to win individual Asian Games golf gold, 15-under 265, plus team silver with Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar). India retained the men's cricket gold, beating Pakistan by 19 runs (India 211/6; Abhishek Sharma 61 off 28, Tilak Varma 51* off 22), and the men's hockey gold, beating Malaysia 5-1 to secure direct qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. Aman Sehrawat won wrestling gold and Antim Panghal took silver.
points.why: Firsts are the most asked sports GK facts: first Indian woman individual recurve gold, first Indian woman golf gold, retained cricket and hockey titles, and the Olympic quota link for LA 2028.

points.t: Union Cabinet clears Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (PM Dhara), outlay Rs 1.86 lakh crore
points.s: The Union Cabinet on September 30 approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme, branded PM Dhara (Developing Harmonised and Accelerated Renewable Energy Access). It strengthens India's Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy across states and UTs, and deploys 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) for grid flexibility. Total outlay: Rs 1,86,405 crore (Rs 1,36,378 crore for InSTS, Rs 50,000 crore for BESS), with Rs 54,082 crore of Central Financial Assistance, targeted for completion by FY 2032-33. Greenfield projects go through Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB), brownfield upgrades on cost-plus basis, with State Transmission Utilities as implementing agencies.
points.why: Scheme-plus-numbers question: name, acronym PM Dhara, 135 GW, 50 GWh BESS, outlay, CFA, and target year; supports the 500 GW by 2030 and 900 GW non-fossil by 2035 goals.

points.t: Uttarakhand publishes final electoral roll after SIR: 71,58,949 voters
points.s: The Election Commission published Uttarakhand's final electoral roll on October 3 after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) that began June 8 with July 1, 2026 as the qualifying date. The final roll lists 71,58,949 electors (37,37,701 men, 34,21,036 women, 212 third gender) across 12,543 polling stations. During claims and objections, 1,29,872 new voters were added and 1,04,708 names deleted. It includes 72,656 voters aged 18-19 and 1,22,892 voters above 80. Those left out can still apply via Form 6 on the ECI Net app or through BLOs.
points.why: SIR is the election-process theme of 2026: know the qualifying date, the draft-to-final timeline (July 14 draft, October 3 final), and Form 6 as the correction mechanism.

points.t: Sitharaman at Kautilya Economic Conclave: fundamentals intact amid global shocks
points.s: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said India has navigated recent global shocks with its fundamentals intact and strengthening, citing 7.8% real GDP growth in Q1 FY27, 4.82% CPI inflation in August, and $766 billion in forex reserves. She attributed the resilience to a decade of fiscal prudence, infrastructure creation, banking reforms and last-mile delivery, defining resilience as absorbing shocks while maintaining growth and retaining policy space for future disruptions.
points.why: Macro-economy numbers are direct current-affairs targets: GDP 7.8%, CPI 4.82%, forex $766 billion, and the Kautilya Economic Conclave as the venue.

points.t: NCW submits 37-point report: gender-neutral child care leave, paid paternity leave, 5 lakh creches by 2030
points.s: The National Commission for Women submitted a 37-point recommendatory report on laws relating to maternity and child care to the Department of Personnel and Training, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, and the Ministry of Labour and Employment. Key recommendations: extend gender-neutral Child Care Leave to the private sector, introduce mandatory paid paternity leave in the private and unorganised sectors, create 5 lakh creche seats by 2030 through a proposed National Childcare Infrastructure Mission, and extend maternity and childcare benefits to informal, gig and platform workers.
points.why: Statutory-body recommendations feed social-policy questions: NCW's legal basis (NCW Act 1990, Section 10), the 5-lakh-creche mission, and the private-sector coverage push.

points.t: Katra-Banihal rail speed raised to 100 kmph; Vande Bharat crosses Chenab and Anji bridges
points.s: The Railway Ministry raised the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal broad-gauge section (part of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link) from 75 kmph to 100 kmph, successfully tested on October 1. Vande Bharat Express (26401/26404) set a record by crossing both the world's highest railway arch bridge, the Chenab Bridge (359 metres above the riverbed), and India's first cable-stayed railway bridge, the Anji Khad Bridge, at 100 kmph.
points.why: Infrastructure facts are fixed GK: Chenab Bridge's 359-metre height, Anji Khad as India's first cable-stayed rail bridge, and the USBRL connection to Kashmir Valley rail link.

points.t: Centre officially names 28 locations and features in Ladakh on Survey of India map
points.s: The Government of India and the UT of Ladakh officially named 28 geographical locations and features in Ladakh according to standard place and feature names on the Survey of India map. The list includes areas such as Gogra and Hot Spring, which were associated with the India-China border tensions. The move aims at accurate identification and public awareness of strategically important geographical features.
points.why: Official naming of strategic border geography is classic India-China border question fodder: note Gogra and Hot Spring and the Survey of India as the naming authority.

points.t: Taiwan receives first two F-16V Block 70 jets from the US
points.s: Taiwan took delivery of the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 fighter jets from the United States, landing at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung on October 2. The jets are part of a 2019-approved $8 billion deal for 66 new-build F-16s from Lockheed Martin, delayed by software and production issues. Taiwan's Defence Minister Wellington Koo said more will arrive before year-end; the delivery came about a week after US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington.
points.why: Defence-procurement current affairs: order year (2019), deal value ($8 billion), manufacturer (Lockheed Martin), and the Taiwan-China-US strategic context.

points.t: Over 700 detained at Jantar Mantar protest demanding CEC's ouster over SIR
points.s: Delhi Police detained more than 700 protesters from Jantar Mantar and nearby areas on Gandhi Jayanti as opposition parties and student organisations demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Former Delhi Chief Minister Atishi was among those detained, and opposition leaders denounced the police action.
points.why: Protest-and-commission questions tie together: the Election Commission's composition (CEC plus ECs), Article 324, and the controversy around SIR.

points.t: Gujarat UCC Bill gets presidential assent; BJP MP backs nationwide Uniform Civil Code
points.s: BJP MP Rahul Sinha backed a nationwide Uniform Civil Code after the Gujarat UCC Bill, 2026 received presidential assent, saying it would first be implemented in BJP-ruled states and then extended. He argued that the country is one and laws should be uniform across it.
points.why: UCC sits at the intersection of Directive Principles (Article 44) and current politics: know which states have enacted UCC-linked bills and the presidential-assent requirement for state bills.

points.t: IAF flies 15 sorties to air-drop 28 tonnes of food in Bihar's Saran amid floods
points.s: The Indian Air Force flew 15 sorties to air-drop 28 tonnes of food packets in Saran district of Bihar as floods affected the region, part of ongoing disaster relief operations.
points.why: Disaster-relief roles of the armed forces recur in exams: IAF's air-drop and HADR (Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief) role, and flood-prone Bihar's river geography.

points.t: Pargat Singh appointed Punjab Congress president as Warring resigns
points.s: Newly appointed Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh met Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot at his Delhi residence. Outgoing chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring handed his formal resignation to Rahul Gandhi, reportedly blaming Sachin Pilot for the change.
points.why: State-unit leadership changes appear in polity current affairs: Pargat Singh is the new Punjab Congress chief, succeeding Amarinder Singh Raja Warring.

points.t: Asian Games Day 13: India reaches 16 gold and 76 medals, stays 5th
points.s: India closed October 2 at the Nagoya Asian Games with 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze (76 total), fifth in the standings. Highlights: the women's hockey team beat China 1-0 (Lalremsiami, 10th minute; Savita Punia saved a penalty stroke) to end a 44-year wait for the women's hockey title and secure an LA 2028 Olympic quota; boxing won a record three golds (Lovlina Borgohain 75kg, Parveen Hooda 65kg, Ankush Panghal 80kg); Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod beat South Korea 5-3 for India's first-ever women's recurve team archery gold; and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal came back from 9-2 down to win 65kg gold 10-9.
points.why: Multi-sport results dominate sports GK: note the firsts (women's recurve team gold, three boxing golds), the 44-year hockey gap since 1982, and the Olympic quota link.

points.t: September GST collections surge 14.7% to Rs 2.04 lakh crore
points.s: Gross GST revenue reached Rs 2.04 lakh crore in September 2026, up 14.7% year-on-year, driven by steady economic activity and pre-festive inventory build-up by businesses ahead of the festive season.
points.why: GST collection figures are recurring economy data points. Remember the amount, the growth rate, and the stated driver (festive inventory build-up).

points.t: Rupee breaches 96 per dollar, hits two-month low
points.s: The rupee fell 0.5% to 96.3150 against the US dollar on October 2, a two-month low, as surging US Treasury yields and persistent foreign institutional investor selling pressured emerging-market currencies broadly.
points.why: Exchange-rate movements test the link between US yields, FPI flows, and the rupee. Note the drivers and the 96-per-dollar breach.

points.t: Q1 FY27 FDI equity inflows rise 6% to $19.8 billion, led by Japan
points.s: Foreign direct investment into Indian equity grew 6% year-on-year to $19.8 billion in the April-June 2026 quarter, led by investments from Japan even as inflows from the United States contracted.
points.why: FDI source-country data is a prelims favourite. Note the quarter, the amount, and that Japan led while US inflows shrank.

points.t: Embraer and Mahindra pick Nagpur for C-390 assembly facility
points.s: Brazil's Embraer and the Mahindra Group have zeroed in on Nagpur as the preferred hub for a prospective assembly line for the C-390 Millennium multi-mission aircraft in India, a boost for the Make in India defence-manufacturing push.
points.why: Defence-industrial partnerships and their locations appear in current-affairs sections. Note the aircraft name, the partners, and the city.

points.t: Goyal meets USTR Greer in Milwaukee as India-US trade deal enters final phase
points.s: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal met US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers' meeting in Milwaukee for a productive discussion on an early interim agreement under the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement. Greer said the talks are in the short strokes with the sticking points identified, and that PM Modi and President Trump may speak very soon; the two leaders had already reviewed bilateral progress on October 1.
points.why: Bilateral trade negotiations link IR and economy: note the forum (G20 Trade Ministers' meet), the BTA framework announced in February, and the interim-deal goal.

points.t: Centre launches three-month 'Reforms Utsav' drive from October 2
points.s: The central government began 'Reforms Utsav', a three-month nationwide drive showcasing about 1,300 reforms of the last 12 years through 1,639 events, starting October 2. Around 454 events are planned for October and 349 for November, with ministries running beneficiary-specific outreach to vulnerable sections such as fishermen, street vendors, coal mine workers and pensioners. Separately, Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Paatil launched the 16-day JJM Reform Utsav (October 2-17) for community upkeep of Jal Jeevan Mission assets.
points.why: New government campaigns with names, durations, and targets are staple prelims material. Remember the 1,300 reforms, 1,639 events, and the Jal Jeevan link.

points.t: Special Gram Sabhas nationwide launch People's Plan Campaign 2026-27
points.s: Special Gram Sabhas were held across the country on October 2, launching the People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 themed 'Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas', under which Gram Panchayats will prepare Gram Panchayat Development Plans for 2027-28 through participatory, evidence-based planning. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj said the meetings would review Finance Commission grants, Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline digital governance, own-source revenue, SVAMITVA property cards, and the Panchayat Advancement Index; the Rural Development Department will highlight the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) with its statutory 125-day wage employment guarantee.
points.why: Panchayati Raj questions hinge on Article 243G, GPDPs, and scheme names. Remember the campaign theme, the target year (GPDPs for 2027-28), SVAMITVA, eGramSwaraj, and the 125-day wage guarantee.

points.t: SIR row escalates: ECI extends revision dates as AAP protests hit Delhi Metro
points.s: The Election Commission of India extended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) schedule for electoral rolls in Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya. Meanwhile, AAP and student groups protested over SIR and alleged mass voter deletions, prompting Delhi Metro to close entry and exit at 11 stations including Rajiv Chowk and Central Secretariat; the INDIA bloc separately announced district-level 'Save Democracy' marches from October 2 to 8 demanding elections through ballot papers.
points.why: Electoral roll revision connects Article 324, the Representation of the People Acts, and EVM debates. Note the two states with extended dates and the ballot-paper demand.

points.t: HDFC Bank appoints Anup Bagchi as CEO for three years
points.s: HDFC Bank, India's largest private lender, will appoint Anup Bagchi as its next chief executive for a period of three years.
points.why: Banking-awareness sections test top appointments. Note the bank (largest private lender) and the three-year term.

points.t: Festive season: Maruti and Hero post strong September dispatches
points.s: Automakers reported strong pre-festive dispatches for September: Maruti Suzuki India's total monthly sales rose 24% to 2.36 lakh units, while Hero MotoCorp posted a 12% rise to 7.66 lakh units.
points.why: Auto sales are used as a high-frequency indicator of domestic demand. Remember the two companies, the growth rates, and the festive-season context.

points.t: Gandhi Jayanti observed on October 2
points.s: October 2 is Gandhi Jayanti, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi (born 1869 in Porbandar), observed as the International Day of Non-Violence. It is one of India's three national holidays; PM Modi paid tribute at Rajghat.
points.why: Static GK that repeats yearly: birth year and place, associated movements, and the UN observance (International Day of Non-Violence, adopted 2007).
